title: Legacy snapshot decoder and shadow projection contract
description: Objective: turn a copied frozen legacy project into production LegacySourceRecord values and a frozen old-to-new shadow projection comparison without test-authored semantic authority. Deliverable: @moe/import snapshot decoder plus explicit projection mapping/comparator and a production read-only CLI/service consumer. NOT in scope: live legacy reads, write-back, dual writes, cutover activation, or portability verdict publication. Measured at HEAD 30458af: buildSourceManifest/applyImport/reconcileImport are public, but all consumers are tests; tests/migration/import/import-determinism.test.ts invents payload {owner:'alice'} from manifest paths, no production decoder exists, and no contract maps imported claims/links/reconciliations to daemon BoardProjection entities. Consumers: task-22cfca91c5134b24aaf3e5734444fb93 and task-4e1fe69630da494eb313e27a4543c5c8. Owned paths: packages/import/** plus a focused production consumer under tools/import/** or scripts/import/**, root script/manifest/lock only if required.
definitionOfDone: A production decoder reads only bytes covered by buildSourceManifest and converts supported legacy files into exact frozen LegacySourceRecord values; malformed, extra, ambiguous, or unsupported bytes return stable import code/layer and never guess a payload.

A versioned shadow-projection contract explicitly maps supported legacy claims/links/blockers to the frozen new projection vocabulary and returns ordered field-level mismatches; missing/unmapped fields remain UNKNOWN or NEEDS_RECONCILIATION and never activate authority.

A production read-only CLI/service composes buildSourceManifest -> decoder -> reconcileImport/shadow comparison against a copied snapshot, verifies source hashes before and after, and performs no source write, mtime change, dual write, or activation.

A committed copied-project corpus contains nonzero real legacy shapes plus exact source manifest/hash expectations; tests assert exact file/record/mismatch counts and mutation-check decoder and comparison guards on the production surface.
pnpm --filter @moe/import typecheck && pnpm --filter @moe/import test plus the focused migration gate exit 0.
taskRails: Do not convert manifest paths into invented records in tests; semantic records must come from the production decoder.
The shadow comparator is advisory/read-only and may not call applyImport with an authority-bearing production store or emit activation commands.
Preserve source bytes and mtimes; all unsupported/ambiguous facts are typed with exact code and layer.

implementationPlan.description: Extend the closed refusal vocabulary in import-contract.ts, first, because everything below asserts against it. IMPORT_REFUSAL_LAYERS is today exactly [INPUT, MANIFEST, CANONICAL, APPLY] and IMPORT_REFUSAL_CODES exactly [IMPORT_COMMIT_FAILED, IMPORT_MANIFEST_EMPTY, IMPORT_RECORD_UNCANONICAL, IMPORT_ROOT_INVALID, IMPORT_SOURCE_UNREADABLE, IMPORT_TOO_LARGE_FOR_ONE_COMMIT] - neither has a member for a DECODE step or for an unsupported/ambiguous legacy shape, so both must gain members. Add a DECODE layer and a SHADOW layer, plus the codes the decoder and comparator need (e.g. IMPORT_SOURCE_UNSUPPORTED for a file shape this version does not decode, IMPORT_SOURCE_AMBIGUOUS for bytes admitting more than one reading, IMPORT_SOURCE_DIGEST_MISMATCH for a file whose bytes no longer match its manifest entry, and a shadow-side code for an unmapped projection field). I MEASURED that no test pins the length of either array - the only references outside import-contract.ts are the re-exports at index.ts:45-46 - so extending them will not redden a sibling sweep. Keep both frozen `as const` and keep refuseImport the single constructor.
implementationPlan.note:
Extended the closed refusal vocabulary. IMPORT_REFUSAL_LAYERS 4 -> 6: added DECODE (between MANIFEST and CANONICAL, pipeline order) and SHADOW (last, advisory). IMPORT_REFUSAL_CODES 6 -> 11: added IMPORT_SHADOW_FIELD_UNMAPPED, IMPORT_SOURCE_AMBIGUOUS, IMPORT_SOURCE_DIGEST_MISMATCH, IMPORT_SOURCE_MALFORMED, IMPORT_SOURCE_UNSUPPORTED (kept alphabetical). Four distinct DECODE codes rather than one "bad file" code, documented so none can stand in for another. Both arrays stay Object.freeze/as const; refuseImport remains the single constructor.

RE-MEASURED the plan's claim myself rather than trusting it (rails: descriptions are stale by default): grep -rn "IMPORT_REFUSAL_CODES\|IMPORT_REFUSAL_LAYERS" over all .ts/.mts/.mjs/.js outside node_modules returns 6 hits, all inside packages/import (import-contract.ts definitions/types + index.ts:45-46 re-exports). Nothing pins either array's length or membership, so extending them reddens no sibling sweep - the frozen-ALL-array hazard does not apply here.

implementationPlan.description: TDD. Add the production decoder in a new focused module: bytes covered by a SourceManifest -> frozen LegacySourceRecord values. Signature takes the already-built manifest plus the root, never a raw directory walk, because DoD-1 says it reads ONLY bytes covered by buildSourceManifest - iterate manifest.entries ({digest, path, size}) and never readdir. CRITICAL GUARD: re-hash each file and compare against its manifest entry digest BEFORE decoding it; a file whose bytes changed since the manifest was built is IMPORT_SOURCE_DIGEST_MISMATCH at layer DECODE, not a record. Produce exactly the landed shape {declaredTime: string|null, kind, legacyId, payload, sourcePath} from import-canonical.ts:26 - declaredTime is whatever the SOURCE declared or null, NEVER a clock read, and payload is parsed from the file bytes, never assembled from the path. A file that is malformed, carries an unsupported shape for this version, or admits more than one reading returns the exact code and layer from step 1 and NO record; the decoder never guesses a payload and never partially emits. Tests assert the exact code AND layer for each refusal arm, and assert an exact record count for a good corpus.
implementationPlan.note:
TDD: wrote legacy-decoder.test.ts first and ran it red ("Cannot find module './legacy-decoder.js'", Tests no tests), then implemented until 12/12 green.

decodeLegacySources({manifest, root}) -> {records, refusals, version}. Read set is manifest.entries ONLY - no readdir, no glob, no path arithmetic beyond join(root, ...entry.path.split("/")). Each entry is re-hashed with sha256Hex and compared to entry.digest BEFORE parsing, so bytes that changed since the manifest cannot get real provenance.

Record shape is exactly import-canonical.ts:26. payload = document MINUS the envelope keys (id, legacyId, time) - which is precisely the semantics tests/migration hand-wrote as {owner:"alice"} beside bytes that already said "owner":"alice". declaredTime is the source's own `time` or null; no clock, no random. kind comes from the directory family (skills->skill, tasks->task) - family selects WHICH decoder applies, the way an extension selects a parser; no payload field is ever derived from the path.

Refusal arms, each pinned by exact code AND layer DECODE: IMPORT_SOURCE_DIGEST_MISMATCH (bytes changed after hashing), IMPORT_SOURCE_UNREADABLE (entry gone), IMPORT_SOURCE_UNSUPPORTED (family/extension this version declines), IMPORT_SOURCE_MALFORMED (non-JSON, non-record, no legacyId, mistyped id/time), IMPORT_SOURCE_AMBIGUOUS (legacyId and older `id` dialect disagree). A file yields a record or a refusal, never both, never partial. Total by construction - no throw path.

Tests include the two controls that stop this being vacuous: the AMBIGUOUS test pairs the two-disagreeing-ids case with a positive control where `id` alone still decodes (so the refusal is about disagreement, not about `id` existing), and the read-set test builds the manifest, THEN writes tasks/smuggled.json, and asserts the record set is unchanged.

Added packages/import/src/legacy-decoder.js bridge (export * from "./legacy-decoder.ts"), matching every sibling module - Node cannot resolve a .js specifier to .ts, and index.ts will import this module in step 4, so tests/runtime/package-loadability.test.ts would fail on the entry probe without it.

implementationPlan.description: TDD. Add the versioned shadow-projection contract and comparator. Declare a SHADOW_PROJECTION_VERSION and an explicit FROZEN target vocabulary for the new-side projection entities, then map supported legacy claims/links/blockers onto it and return ORDERED field-level mismatches. READ planningNotes.approachesConsidered before writing this: the comparator deliberately compares over PLAIN DATA the caller supplies, and does NOT import the daemon's BoardProjection - @moe/import declares zero dependencies, BoardProjection exists only in apps/daemon, and nothing in the repo depends on @moe/daemon, so importing it would invert the dependency graph from a pure leaf onto the top-level app. Mismatch ordering must be total and deterministic (sort by entity kind, then id, then field name) so two runs over identical bytes produce identical output - the package has no clock and no random source and must keep it that way. A legacy field with no mapping stays UNKNOWN or NEEDS_RECONCILIATION and never activates authority; an unmapped field is reported with the exact shadow code and layer, never silently dropped. Keep this file at or under 250 physical lines; if it would exceed, move the vocabulary into import-contract.ts (already an owned path) rather than adding a tenth file, because this plan is exactly at the 10-file cap.
implementationPlan.note:
TDD. SHADOW_PROJECTION_VERSION = "moe-shadow-projection/1". Frozen target vocabulary: SHADOW_ENTITY_KINDS [BLOCKER, CLAIM, LINK]; SHADOW_ENTITY_FIELDS per kind; SHADOW_MISMATCH_KINDS (ENTITY_ABSENT_ON_CURRENT/LEGACY, FIELD_ABSENT_ON_CURRENT/LEGACY, FIELD_DIFFERS, FIELD_UNMAPPED); SHADOW_DISPOSITIONS is exactly [NEEDS_RECONCILIATION, UNKNOWN] with a frozen kind->disposition map, so no arm can activate authority - same structural technique as ImportedClaimStatus having no ACTIVE arm.

projectLegacyImport({claims, links}) maps claims -> CLAIM, a SUSPENDED claim additionally -> BLOCKER (the legacy hold, derived from the claim's own status so it cannot outlive it), links -> LINK whose id is canonicalDigest over the whole tuple, not a joined key. compareShadowProjections(legacy, current) takes PLAIN DATA on both sides per planningNotes - no @moe/daemon import, so the leaf package's zero dependencies stay zero and the comparator cannot reach an authority-bearing store by construction.

Unmapped fields are reported on BOTH surfaces from one computation: an ordered FIELD_UNMAPPED mismatch AND a typed refuseImport("IMPORT_SHADOW_FIELD_UNMAPPED", "SHADOW"). An entity whose KIND the vocabulary does not declare is also reported rather than dropped out of the kind-keyed walk.

DEVIATION FROM THE PLAN, disclosed with the measurement that forced it. Step 3 said keep the file <=250 lines and, if it would exceed, move the vocabulary into import-contract.ts rather than adding a file. Written as one module it measured 313 lines (grep -c ''). I measured the plan's escape valve instead of assuming it: import-contract.ts is 223 lines after step 1 and the vocabulary block is ~80, so that move produces ~303 lines - it trades one over-target file for another. I therefore split the vocabulary into packages/import/src/shadow-contract.ts (111 lines) and left the mapper/comparator in shadow-projection.ts (234). Epic rail 5 makes this the sanctioned fix ("per-file violations remain real and are fixed by splitting the file"), and the 10-file plan cap is a plan-shape threshold at submit time, not a completion gate. Net: no production file over the 250 target.

Ordering is total over (entityKind, entityId, field, mismatchKind) and is LOAD-BEARING, not decorative: a held claim yields a CLAIM and a BLOCKER sharing one id, so a sort keyed on id alone is not total. Mismatches are emitted in caller-supplied order and sorted afterwards, and the suite compares a forward run against a reversed-input run - which is what makes drill [4] able to redden rather than being an equivalent mutant under V8's stable sort.

Also asserted: exact ordered mismatch key lists, exact legacy/current value pairs, disposition == the frozen map for every mismatch, refusal code+layer exact, link-id collision control (from "a"/to "b:c" vs from "a:b"/to "c" get different ids), and an all-agree positive control returning zero mismatches and zero refusals - without which a comparator that flagged everything would still satisfy the counts.

implementationPlan.description: Add the read-only production CLI under tools/import/ and make it typechecked. IMPORT STYLE IS FORCED, do not fight it: pnpm-workspace.yaml globs only `apps/*` and `packages/*`, so tools/ is NOT a workspace package and a bare `@moe/import` specifier will not resolve. Follow the tools/packaging precedent exactly - it imports `../../packages/contracts/src/distribution/distribution-contract.js` by deep relative path - so use `../../packages/import/src/index.js`. Then add a root `typecheck:import` script mirroring the existing `typecheck:packaging`, naming the tools/import file(s) explicitly with the same flag set (--strict --module nodenext --moduleResolution nodenext --target es2024 --lib es2024 --types node --exactOptionalPropertyTypes --noUncheckedIndexedAccess --verbatimModuleSyntax). That explicit-file form is exactly why the deep relative import does not trip TS6059: there is no --project and no rootDir to fall outside of. The CLI composes buildSourceManifest -> decoder -> reconcileImport/shadow comparison against a COPIED snapshot, verifies the source hashes before AND after the run, and performs no write of any kind. Per task rail 2 it must not call applyImport with an authority-bearing production store and must emit no activation command.
implementationPlan.note:
tools/import/import-shadow.ts composes the real chain: buildSourceManifest -> decodeLegacySources -> deriveProvenance -> reconcileImport -> projectLegacyImport -> compareShadowProjections, printing one deterministic JSON report. Deep relative specifier "../../packages/import/src/index.js" exactly as tools/packaging does, and root script typecheck:import mirrors typecheck:packaging flag for flag, naming both tools/import files explicitly (no --project, no rootDir, so no TS6059). pnpm typecheck:import exit 0.

Claims and links are derived through PRODUCTION applyImport rather than restated in the tool - a second copy of that derivation is how a shadow starts disagreeing with the importer it shadows. Task rail 2 is satisfied structurally: the port is a DISCARDING_STORE literal holding no database, file, socket or handle, so no authority-bearing store is reachable, and the file emits no command of any kind. maxEventsPerCommit is finite (10_000) on purpose - an unbounded value would let the shadow accept a snapshot the real importer refuses.

Read-only is asserted on BYTES, not promised: observeSources() captures digest + mtimeMs + size for EVERY manifest entry before the run and again after, and driftBetween() names the exact file and which of the three moved. Any drift refuses IMPORT_SOURCE_DIGEST_MISMATCH at MANIFEST. Ban-grep for write calls over tools/*.ts returns 0 hits, and I ran the POSITIVE CONTROL for that grep (same pattern hits packages/import/src/legacy-decoder.test.ts and source-manifest.test.ts), so the zero is a measurement rather than a broken pattern. git status over packages/import/corpus after a real CLI run shows only the untracked-directory entry - no modification.

Exercised arms: good run on the corpus exit 0 (9 sourceFiles, 6 records, 3 decodeRefusals, 4 reconciliations, 10 mismatches, 0 shadowRefusals, verifiedFiles 9, manifestDigest d1ab82e6...); no operands exit 2 with IMPORT_ROOT_INVALID/INPUT; a malformed --current file exit 1 with IMPORT_SOURCE_MALFORMED/INPUT. The untrusted new-side projection is structurally validated before it can reach the comparator, so junk cannot be coerced into confident mismatches.

TWO DEVIATIONS, both forced and disclosed.
(1) FILE SPLIT. Written as one file the CLI measured 318 lines, over the 250 target, so the untrusted-input boundary (argv parsing + the --current projection reader) moved to tools/import/shadow-input.ts. Now 239 + 96. Epic rail 5 names splitting the file as the fix for a per-file overrun.
(2) A .js BRIDGE INSIDE tools/. The split introduced the first intra-tools import in the repo, and it broke at RUNTIME while tsc stayed green: `Cannot find module D:\projexts\moe-next\tools\import\shadow-input.js` - Node does not resolve a .js specifier to .ts, and unlike packages/* the tools/ tree had no bridges (tools/packaging's two files never import each other, so the repo had no precedent). Caught only because I ran the CLI rather than trusting typecheck:import - the plan's own reasoning that an untypechecked production file is a real defect cuts both ways here.

implementationPlan.description: Add the corpus-driven gate that proves the REAL production path, in packages/import/src so the package test script collects it. It must obtain its records from the production decoder - per task rail 1, semantic records may not be hand-authored in a test. This is the exact defect that motivated the task: tests/migration/import/import-determinism.test.ts:70 hand-writes `payload: { owner: "alice" }` while its own fixture bytes at line 40 already contain `"owner":"alice"`, so the test authored semantics the decoder should derive. Assert EXACT counts, not lower bounds: the exact number of manifest files, the exact number of decoded records, the exact number of refusals per code, and the exact number of ordered mismatches - and assert the counts are nonzero, because a sweep that silently produces zero cases passes while testing nothing. Assert the byte-level read-only property directly: capture every corpus file's digest AND mtime before the CLI runs and re-assert both afterwards, so a source write or an mtime touch fails the gate. Do NOT edit tests/migration/import/import-determinism.test.ts - it is outside this task's owned paths; record its invented-payload defect as a named follow-up instead.
implementationPlan.note:
Corpus gate at packages/import/src/legacy-shadow.test.ts (261 lines), collected by the package script. 9 tests, all green; full package suite now 7 files / 84 tests green.

EVERY record comes out of the production decoder. The test hands production nothing it authored - task rail 1 holds by construction, since the only inputs are the committed corpus bytes.

EXACT, NONZERO counts (never lower bounds): 9 manifest files with per-file digest AND size hand-transcribed and compared as one array, manifest digest d1ab82e6...; 6 decoded records; 3 decode refusals asserted as an exact [path, code, layer] list, one per code (UNSUPPORTED/AMBIGUOUS/MALFORMED, all at DECODE); 4 reconciliations asserted as an exact [sourcePath, ambiguityClass] list; CLI counts asserted with toEqual over the WHOLE counts object (decodeRefusals 3, mismatches 10, reconciliations 4, records 6, shadowRefusals 0, sourceFiles 9, verifiedFiles 9) so a new count key cannot appear unnoticed.

The anti-invented-payload assertion is specific rather than structural: tasks/alpha.json decodes to {owner:"ada", priority:"high"} - `priority` appears in the bytes and in no path component, so a path-derived payload cannot produce it.

Shadow leg runs over REAL decoded records: decode -> applyImport (discarding port) -> projectLegacyImport gives 6 CLAIM + 1 BLOCKER + 3 LINK, and the new side is a PERTURBATION of that projection (drop the blocker, change one principal, add an unmapped `tier`). The comparison must report exactly three mismatches in declared order [BLOCKER * ENTITY_ABSENT_ON_CURRENT, CLAIM principal FIELD_DIFFERS, CLAIM tier FIELD_UNMAPPED] plus exactly one IMPORT_SHADOW_FIELD_UNMAPPED/SHADOW refusal - the five untouched claims and three untouched links reporting NOTHING is what separates this from a comparator that flags everything. A reversed-entity-order run must produce byte-identical mismatches.

Read-only asserted on bytes: digest+size+mtimeMs for all 9 files captured before spawning the CLI as a REAL child process (process.execPath, the repo's existing probe pattern) and re-asserted after, plus a re-run of buildSourceManifest to confirm the tree still hashes to the pinned digest. A write that restores identical content still moves mtime and would fail here.

Also pinned: no corpus file contains byte 0x0D. .gitattributes is `* text=auto eol=lf`, so a CRLF-mangled checkout would otherwise break all nine digests with a failure that says nothing about line endings.

FOLLOW-UP RECORDED, NOT SILENTLY FIXED. tests/migration/import/import-determinism.test.ts:65-73 still derives its records from manifest paths and hand-writes payload {owner:"alice"} while its fixture bytes at line 40 already carry "owner":"alice". That file is outside this task's owned paths, so it is untouched. Recorded here, in the gate's header comment, and in the task handoff memory.

implementationPlan.description: Run the mutation drills DoD-4 requires, against the PRODUCTION surface rather than a test helper, and record that each reddens a NAMED assertion before restoring. [1] Make the decoder skip its manifest-digest comparison so a tampered file decodes anyway - the digest-mismatch refusal test must go red on its exact code, not merely 'threw'. [2] Make the decoder fall back to deriving a payload field from the sourcePath when the bytes lack it - the decoded-payload assertion must go red, which is the production-side guard against the invented-payload defect this task exists to fix. [3] Make the comparator drop an unmapped field instead of reporting it - the ordered-mismatch count assertion must go red. [4] Make the comparator's ordering non-total (e.g. sort by id only) - the deterministic-ordering assertion must go red. For each: confirm the drill actually applied (print the replaced line range and chain with &&, since a drill that applied nothing reads as green), read the failure MESSAGE rather than the count (over-reddening means a broken environment, not a strong test), restore with Edit rather than git checkout (checkout reverts to HEAD, destroying uncommitted work), and hash-check the file back to its pre-drill bytes before the next drill.
implementationPlan.note:
Four drills, all against the PRODUCTION surface, each recorded with the named assertion it reddened and each restored by Edit (never git checkout - these files are UNTRACKED, so a checkout restore would delete them outright rather than revert them). Pre-drill sha256: legacy-decoder.ts eb4dd59f40dcebe913416584e40144fff707743d8680d40c16eabf65eda0ebe6, shadow-projection.ts 464302b7e14a84138eefe0fc9f98d4ebf04a95fa975b28f86b394ee4dc0bd0fd. Both hashes re-verified identical after the last restore, and the full package suite is back to 7 files / 84 tests green.

FIX FIRST, so a drill could not redden for the wrong reason. Two decoder refusal tests reached their code assertion through a lookup helper that THROWS when no refusal exists, so drill [1] would have reddened on "no refusal for tasks/alpha.json" - a helper throw, not an outcome. Both now assert the whole refusal list as [sourcePath, code, layer] tuples. That is why drill [1]'s failure below reads as a value diff.

[1] DECODER SKIPS THE DIGEST COMPARISON. `const digest = sha256Hex(bytes)` -> `const digest = entry.digest` at line 106 (applied hash 8f505afa...). RED, exactly 1 of 12: "refuses a file whose bytes changed after the manifest hashed them", AssertionError expected [] to deeply equal [["tasks/alpha.json","IMPORT_SOURCE_DIGEST_MISMATCH","DECODE"]]. The exact code and layer, and no over-reddening.

[2] DECODER INVENTS A PAYLOAD FIELD FROM THE PATH. payload -> Object.freeze({...readPayload(document), slug: entry.path}) at line 206 (applied hash 09d1a366...). RED 4 tests across two suites: the decoder's exact-payload list (+ "slug": "tasks/alpha.json"), the corpus gate's tasks/alpha.json payload (expected {owner:'ada',priority:'high'}), the reconciliation count (expected 10 to be 4 - the invented field becomes an UNKNOWN_FIELD per record, a real downstream consequence), and the CLI counts object. This is the production-side guard against the invented-payload defect the task exists to remove, and it is now load-bearing in four places.

[3] COMPARATOR DROPS AN UNMAPPED FIELD. Deleted the reportUnmapped call from compareFields (applied hash f5924bc2...). RED 3: the ordered mismatch list in the unit suite, the "exact shadow code and layer" test (expected +0 to be 1 refusal), and the corpus gate's three-element perturbation list.

[4] COMPARATOR ORDERING MADE NON-TOTAL. Removed the entityKind leg from compareMismatches, leaving id first (applied hash 889bc0e2...). RED 2, both ordering assertions: "orders identically however the caller ordered the entities it supplied" and the gate's "reports exactly the perturbation, in the declared total order". Worth recording WHY this one is not an equivalent mutant: V8's sort is stable, so an id-only sort would preserve emission order and change nothing if mismatches were emitted in kind order. They are emitted in caller-supplied order and sorted afterwards, and a held claim yields a CLAIM and a BLOCKER sharing one id - which is what gives the drill something real to break. I designed for that in step 3 rather than discovering it here.

Every failure message was read rather than the failure count: each drill reddened between 1 and 4 tests, all naming the assertion the mutation targeted. No drill produced a suite-wide collapse, which would have meant a broken environment rather than a strong test.

implementationPlan.note:
Adversarial review found TWO REAL DEFECTS in my own diff, both fixed, tested and drilled - not filed as theoretical.

DEFECT A - a `__proto__` field was silently dropped AND poisoned the payload. Measured, not reasoned: JSON.parse gives `__proto__` an OWN property, but the accumulator's `payload[key] = document[key]` hits the inherited setter, so Object.keys(payload) came back ["owner"] from bytes carrying {"__proto__":...,"owner":"ada"}, AND Object.getPrototypeOf(payload) !== Object.prototype. The second half is the worse one: a moved prototype fails isPlainRecord, so canonicalPayload refuses and the record is reported CORRUPT_BYTES for a reason no operator could see - a silent drop in a package whose whole promise is never dropping a record. Fixed with Object.fromEntries (CreateDataPropertyOrThrow defines an own property). Same bug existed at the CLI's untrusted-input parser (tools/import/shadow-input.ts) and is fixed identically.

DEFECT B - `fields[field] ?? null` is wrong for exactly one field name. Reading an ABSENT `__proto__` returns the prototype OBJECT rather than undefined, so `??` never fires and a non-string escapes into typed mismatch output. Both projections are caller-supplied plain data, so the key is reachable. Fixed with Object.hasOwn.

HARDENING C - the decoder takes the manifest as a PARAMETER. buildSourceManifest never emits an escaping path, but a hand-built manifest with `../`, a leading slash or a drive letter would have made join() read outside the frozen tree with full provenance. Now refused IMPORT_SOURCE_UNREADABLE/DECODE, reusing the existing segment-wise escapesSkillDirectory rather than writing a second path-escape test.

All three are drilled, each reddening its own named assertion, each restored and hash-verified (legacy-decoder.ts 94068b71..., shadow-projection.ts 46c6d63d...): [A] revert to the assignment loop -> "keeps a field named __proto__ as an ordinary payload field", expected ['owner'] to deeply equal ['__proto__','owner']. [B] revert to `?? null` -> "treats an absent __proto__ field as absent rather than as the prototype", expected {...(12)} to be null. [C] disable the guard -> "refuses a manifest entry that points outside the frozen tree".

planningNotes.approachesConsidered:
THE PROJECTION VOCABULARY - the most contestable decision here, flagged for QA. DoD-2 says the contract maps legacy facts to 'the frozen new projection vocabulary', and the daemon's BoardProjection is the obvious reading. REJECTED: @moe/import declares zero dependencies and is a pure leaf; BoardProjection lives only in apps/daemon, which is the TOP of the dependency graph with 8 workspace deps. Adding @moe/daemon to @moe/import would invert the graph and create a cycle risk the moment the daemon wants to consume the importer. CHOSEN: the shadow contract declares its OWN explicitly versioned frozen target vocabulary and the comparator compares over PLAIN DATA the caller supplies. The named consumer tasks (task-22cfca91c5134b24aaf3e5734444fb93, task-4e1fe69630da494eb313e27a4543c5c8) can depend on both sides and do the wiring. This also satisfies task rail 2 directly - a comparator that takes data rather than a live store cannot reach an authority-bearing store by construction. RESIDUAL, stated rather than claimed away: the declared vocabulary can drift from the real BoardProjection. That is why it is VERSIONED - drift becomes a visible version mismatch at the consumer rather than a silent disagreement. If QA wants a literal import instead, that is a dependency-direction decision above this task's pay grade and should be routed, not patched in here.

CLI LOCATION. Owned paths offer tools/import/** or scripts/import/**. CHOSEN tools/import, because tools/packaging is the live precedent for a typechecked standalone .ts tool and scripts/ currently holds only .mjs release scripts. Putting the CLI inside packages/import/src instead would have avoided the root package.json edit entirely, but the task explicitly names tools/ or scripts/, and an untypechecked production file would be a real defect - hence the paired typecheck:import script.

CORPUS LOCATION. Owned paths do NOT include tests/migration, yet DoD-4 wants a committed corpus and DoD-5 names 'the focused migration gate'. CHOSEN: corpus at packages/import/corpus/** with its gate test at packages/import/src/legacy-shadow.test.ts - both inside owned paths - while tests/migration/import is RUN unchanged as the pre-existing gate. This keeps the task inside its declared boundary instead of quietly widening it. Corpus sits outside src deliberately: the package test script is `vitest run --root ../.. packages/import/src`, so corpus files under src risk being collected.

NOT SPLIT. 10 distinct files and 9 steps sit at the file cap but under both hard thresholds (>12 steps / >10 files reject). Splitting was considered and rejected: the CLI in DoD-3 composes BOTH the decoder and the comparator and the corpus in DoD-4 serves both, so a split produces three tasks with a two-way join at the end - strictly worse than one coherent task. Note there is ZERO slack at 10 files: if shadow-projection.ts would exceed 250 lines, move its vocabulary into import-contract.ts (already owned) rather than adding an eleventh file.

That is the usual hazard with a frozen ALL array and it does NOT apply here.

DEPENDENCY TOPOLOGY, the finding that shapes the design. packages/import/package.json declares ZERO dependencies. BoardProjection exists ONLY in apps/daemon/src/projections/** - not in @moe/core, not in any package. @moe/daemon IS a consumable workspace package (exports './src/index.ts') but NOTHING depends on it; it sits at the top of the graph with 8 workspace deps of its own.

TOOLS/ IS NOT A WORKSPACE PACKAGE. pnpm-workspace.yaml globs only `apps/*` and `packages/*`. tools/packaging/distribution-build.ts therefore imports by DEEP RELATIVE path (`../../packages/contracts/src/distribution/distribution-contract.js`) and is typechecked by the root `typecheck:packaging` script, which names its files EXPLICITLY with flags and no --project. planningNotes.risks:
ZERO FILE-COUNT SLACK. The plan is exactly at the 10 distinct-file cap. Any new file rejects the plan. The escape valve is import-contract.ts, which is already owned and already being edited.

DETERMINISM IS THE PACKAGE'S WHOLE CLAIM. index.ts states there is no clock and no random source anywhere in @moe/import, because either makes the 'identical bytes produce identical canonical hashes' property unprovable. The decoder must take declaredTime from the SOURCE or null - never a clock read - and the comparator's mismatch ordering must be TOTAL, including for equal sort keys, or two runs over identical bytes can disagree. Re-grep the new modules for Date/now/random in adversarial review.

THE DECODER CAN SILENTLY WIDEN ITS READ SET. DoD-1 restricts it to bytes covered by buildSourceManifest. A readdir, a glob, a parent-relative path or a symlink escaping the corpus all violate that while looking like ordinary file access. Iterate manifest.entries only, and re-hash each file against its entry before decoding - otherwise the decoder is trusting bytes the manifest never covered.

READ-ONLY MUST BE ASSERTED ON BYTES, NOT PROMISED IN PROSE. Capture digest AND mtime for EVERY corpus file before and after, not just the first - an mtime change from an accidental write-mode open is exactly the kind of violation a digest-only check misses.

MUTATION DRILL HAZARDS, all previously observed on this board: a drill that applied nothing reads as green (print the replaced line range, chain with &&); a drill can redden for the WRONG reason (read the message, not the count - over-reddening means a broken env); restoring with git checkout reverts to HEAD and destroys uncommitted work, so restore with Edit and hash-check between drills.

MULTI-LEG GATE MASKING. This task has three separate verification legs (package typecheck+test, typecheck:import, tests/migration). A chained run can exit 0 while one leg is red - read every summary line rather than the final code.

SHARED WORKTREE. Live peers are committing throughout this session (HEAD moved twice while planning). Commit by explicit pathspec only; scratch and drill files must be gone before completion or a foreign whole-tree commit hook can sweep them into another task's commit.

OUT-OF-SCOPE TEMPTATION. tests/migration/import/import-determinism.test.ts contains the invented-payload defect that motivated this task, but it is NOT in owned paths. Fix it as a named follow-up, not silently here.
